definition: Grouping unlabeled documents or sentences by topic or meaning using embedding similarity.
details: Grouping unlabeled documents or sentences by topic or meaning using embedding similarity. It supports discovery, deduplication, and corpus exploration without predefined labels.

explainer.lead: Text clustering groups unlabeled documents or sentences by topic or meaning using embedding similarity. It matters because it supports discovery, deduplication, and corpus exploration without predefined labels.

tiers.eli5: It is like tipping out a box of unsorted photos and letting similar ones naturally pile up together, with no labels to start from.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers embed documents and group them by embedding similarity when no labels exist, then inspect the clusters. The pitfall is assuming clusters map cleanly onto meaningful topics without checking.
tiers.paperLevel: Grouping unlabeled documents or sentences by topic or meaning using embedding similarity; it requires no predefined labels and is intended for discovery, deduplication, and corpus exploration.

explainer.example: A large collection of support emails is embedded and grouped so similar requests cluster together for review.
